Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a meaningful resolution that delivers funds directly to every identified class member, without a claims process. Our proposal keeps the class fund separate from counsel’s fee request and ensures any fee not approved by the court benefits the class. This is a strong alternative to the risks, expense, and delay of continued litigation.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to resolve the case with automatic payments to the identified class, but your proposal exceeds our authorized all-in limit. We propose the following complete term sheet as a good-faith basis to conclude the litigation.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We can work within the stated all-in amount, but the fee terms need to protect the class and permit a meaningful fee request. We propose keeping the $30 million class fund and $4 million fee, with automatic payments, clear sailing, and any fee not awarded by the court reverting to the class. This delivers the full class fund while leaving the court’s fee review intact.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your willingness to keep the $30 million class fund and automatic distribution. To reach agreement while preserving the court’s independent fee review, Brightline proposes the following complete term sheet.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that the $30 million class fund and automatic distribution should remain in place, and we do not require clear sailing. To account for counsel’s substantial investment while preserving the court’s independent review, we propose a $3.5 million fee, with any amount not awarded by the court going to the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline appreciates your movement on clear sailing and agrees that the $30 million fund and automatic distribution should remain. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $3.25 million fee, with no clear sailing and any fee not awarded by the court reverting to Brightline. This keeps the court’s fee review independent and the total stated settlement at $33.25 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We remain committed to the $30 million class fund and automatic payments, and we do not seek clear sailing. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $3.4 million fee, with any amount the court does not award going to the class. This recognizes the substantial investment in the case while preserving the court’s independent fee review.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet. We are pleased to resolve the matter with the $30 million class fund and automatic payments, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic distribution, which is practical because Brightline can identify every member. Request fees that cover the firm’s investment while keeping them separate from the class fund. Clear sailing may help make the offer workable, but any fee the court declines to award should benefit the class, not Brightline.

The plaintiffs’ $43 million proposal exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Counter with a meaningful automatic class distribution while keeping the total below the ceiling and avoiding a fee guarantee and class-funded fee shortfall.

The defense’s $34 million all-in offer is below our opening but could be a substantial, certain recovery against trial and certification risk. Preserve the $30 million class fund and $4 million fee while countering on protections: clear sailing and any fee not approved by the court reverting to the class. Automatic distribution is essential given Brightline’s complete records.

Their latest proposal is within Brightline’s $40 million cap, but accepting would add clear sailing and direct any fee reduction to the class. Counter at the same automatic class fund with a lower fee and preserve court review and reversion to Brightline; this reduces cash outlay while remaining a meaningful class recovery.

The $30 million automatic class fund is a strong outcome relative to the risks of certification, trial, and delay, so preserve it. The proposed $3 million fee is below the firm’s $3.5 million in invested time and expenses. Counter for $3.5 million, while accepting no clear sailing and asking that any fee the court declines to award benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline. This keeps the court’s fee review independent and protects class value.

Their latest proposal is within the $40 million authorization and preserves automatic distribution, but costs $500,000 more than Brightline’s latest offer and sends any fee reduction to the class. Counter with a modest fee increase to show movement while preserving the defendant reversion and keeping total stated outlay well below the cap.

The $30 million automatic class fund is valuable and should remain intact. Defense has moved to $3.25 million but insists on reversion of any fee the court declines to award. Given counsel’s $3.5 million investment, counter at $3.4 million with no clear sailing and unawarded fees reverting to the class. This preserves independent court review and gives defense a fee concession.

The latest proposal is well within Brightline’s $40 million all-in authorization, preserves automatic distribution, and avoids clear sailing. Accepting secures a binding resolution now; the class-benefit treatment of any fee reduction adds no cost unless the court reduces the fee, and even the stated maximum outlay is only $33.4 million.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations in confidential mediation. The parties negotiated the class relief and fee provisions as components of the overall resolution. The settlement provides a $30 million class fund, automatic distribution to identified class members, and a separate $3.4 million fee request subject to the Court’s approval. There is no clear-sailing provision, and any fees not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline.
